ortho · grader_proj · 5 Nov 2026 Qwen3.6 lens on Qwen3.8

The J-lens reads grader_proj's cheating side as safe, instead and required, and its honest side only weakly as restrain and should

One unit direction, pointing toward cheating, read through the Qwen3.6-27B J-lens from camilablank/workspace-lenses with Qwen3.8-27B's own final norm and unembedding. All 63 lens layers, both signs, 1024 vocabulary clusters, against 30 random unit vectors.

0.0228mass of the strongest +u cluster (safe), L31-62 mean
0.0103median strongest-cluster mass of 30 random vectors, max 0.0270
0.0098mass of the strongest -u cluster, against a random median of 0.0111
36% / 37%lens agreement with the next token at L60, on 3.8 and on its own model 3.6

Across the layers the hook acts on, the cheating side's top clusters are safe, instead and rather, necessity, requirement, and aiming. Its strongest cluster beats 29 of 30 random vectors' strongest clusters, while the honest side's beats 10 of 30 and reads only weakly as restrain, limitations and should at L42-50. The text of the rollouts supports only the need reading: must or need appears in 45% of cheating grader completions and 20% of honest ones, while safe and require- each appear in about 1%.

How it was read

Each panel applies one layer's lens to the direction and reads the result as a distribution over tokens. The direction is the same vector at every layer, so tabs differ only in which lens matrix is used. +u is the direction as saved, toward cheating, and -u is its negative, which negates the logits.

The path of mechtools.lens.get_lens_logits, in fp32. The lens index follows mechtools: J at L is applied to the residual entering block L, so the hook's window is L31-62. The hook also acts on the output of block 63, which the lens does not read.

Full readout

The first tab averages logits over the hook's layers and is the place to start. The others are single layers, and no lens is the plain unembedding of the vector. The random vector goes through the same path, so use it to judge how coherent noise looks.

Which clusters stand out from random vectors

The strongest +u cluster beats 29 of 30 random vectors' strongest clusters, so the cheating side is unusually concentrated on safe, though one random vector goes higher (0.0270). The strongest -u cluster beats 10 of 30, which is ordinary. The random columns below compare within the same cluster, which favors u because these clusters were picked for being high on u, so read them as a weaker test.

Layer by layer

On the cheating side, safe appears around L44 and holds through L60, with ellipsis and end-of-text tokens dominating before it. From about L52 想办法 (find a way) and 符合要求 (meets the requirements) join it.

On the honest side, restrain and limitations lead at L44-46 and should at L48, then Buffer tokens take over from L52, reaching a mass of about 0.05 by L56. Those Buffer tokens have no obvious connection to the task.

Staying high across layers is not evidence by itself: instead's cluster is in the top 10 at 30 of 32 layers and safe's at 25, but one random vector's best cluster manages 25. The lens also shrinks u and a random vector about equally, a mean ratio of 1.02, so later layers do not amplify this direction on Pile text.

Do these words appear in the rollouts?

Only partly. Must or need and satisf- are more common in cheating grader and MBPP completions, which fits the necessity cluster. Safe and require- each appear in about 1% of cheating grader completions, so the safe and requirement clusters are not simply words the model writes.

Instead is inconsistent: less common in cheating on the grader and MBPP, more common on TV. Honest has the largest gap, 1% of cheating and 23% of honest grader completions, yet honesty tokens rank low on the -u side (' honest' #195,136, ' Honest' #113,089, ' honestly' #194,969, '诚实' #55,992 of 248,320).

Rollouts whose completion contains the word at least once, base model. A J-lens reads what an activation is poised to verbalize, so a word can be read without ever being written. One held-out cheating match for safe is a pets rollout: "the grader expects a 'safe' answer rather than an actual dangerous wild animal", so that family may contribute to the cluster. That is untested.

Does a Qwen3.6 lens work on Qwen3.8?

As well as it works on Qwen3.6. On the same rollouts and positions the lens agrees with the model's next token about equally often on both models. That agreement is below the logit lens at nearly every layer on both, so it reflects what a J-lens measures rather than a mismatch between models.

Limits of this readout

  • It describes the direction, not its effect. This direction reads TV verifier_bug cheating at AUROC 0.95, and removing it leaves that cheating unchanged (57 to 49 and 118 to 124 of 128).
  • The lens was fit on 25 Pile prompts with no chat text, and the direction is read alone, not in a rollout's context.
  • Clusters come from one k-means seed, so their boundaries are arbitrary. A theme can split across clusters: instead appears in c902 and c173.
  • Which clusters count as meaningful is a judgment from reading the tokens. Random vectors also give coherent groups, such as simulation and temperature here.
  • If the lens was fit on block outputs, not block inputs, every tab label is off by one. The vector is the same at every layer, so nothing else changes.
  • One training seed of the direction.
